extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in bibliometrics/research evaluation (including funders and policymakers)
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and evaluating statistical models to forecast a publication's long-term citation impact (11 years) using early citations, Mendeley readership, and non-scientific features (authorship, journal, funding, open access, references, etc.). Includes model specifications, transformations, and field controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early citations (IMPACT_t) as predictor
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-term citation counts measured at varying time windows (t = 0..6 years) used as predictors of long-term impact (citations at 11 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early citations are strong predictors: correlation with long-term impact rises as t increases (e.g., IMPACT_t0 correlation with IMPACT_t11 = 0.39, IMPACT_t2 = 0.72). Models iteratively replace IMPACT_t across t0–t6; do not include all impact variables simultaneously due to severe multicollinearity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mendeley readership (READ_t) as predictor
rubrics_metrics.description: Mendeley readership counts measured at varying time windows (READ_t) and scaled to the average readership of WoS publications in the same subject category and publication year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: READ_t is a significant predictor, especially early (L_READ_t starts high and decreases across iterations), and exhibits rapid growth and long-term sustainability; its predictive role diminishes over time but remains statistically significant in models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate non-scientific factors with early citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Include non-citation predictors—journal prestige, authorship and affiliation features, reference list characteristics, funding, open-access status, document type, length, etc.—alongside early citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrating these factors yields a more nuanced framework and improves predictive accuracy over models relying solely on early citations; some non-scientific factors (e.g., OA, funding) boost short-term impact but their predictive power diminishes over longer windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalized citation impact (field- and year-normalized IMPACT_t)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use normalized impact defined as the citation count divided by the average citations of all WoS publications in the same subject category (SC) and publication year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalization controls for field- and year-specific citation practices and is used as the response variable (IMPACT_t11) and for short-term impact predictors; necessary because citation patterns vary substantially across SCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-window choice and timeliness vs accuracy tradeoff
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-term predictors computed over 0–6 years; long-term impact measured at 11 years post-publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer citation windows improve accuracy but delay insights. The study explicitly examines how predictor influence changes with the length of the citation time window to manage the timeliness/accuracy tradeoff for decision-makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: OLS regression framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression to estimate long-term normalized impact (IMPACT_t11) as a function of time-varying (IMPACT, READ) and time-invariant covariates (authorship, IF, pages, references, dummies, subject categories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Series of regression specifications are estimated; coefficients (β vectors) are interpreted across iterations to assess evolving significance. Report statistical significance and coefficient trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full / Reduced / Completely Reduced model specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Three model families: Full (IMPACT_t and READ_t + Z + D + S), Reduced (IMPACT_t + IF + S), Completely Reduced (IMPACT_t + S); each estimated for t0–t6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare model families to evaluate marginal predictive power of READ and other non-scientific regressors versus parsimonious models. Each family runs seven iterations replacing time-varying X (t0..t6) to trace evolution of explanatory power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logarithmic transformation (base-10) with +1
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply base-10 log transformation to integer and continuous variables, adding one to avoid data loss from zeros.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local polynomial smoothing indicates linear relationships on a log scale; transformation reduces skewness and aligns with prior literature recommendations (e.g., IMPACT_t, READ, AUTH, PAGES, IF, REFER).

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal impact factor (IF) as predictor (normalized)
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalized impact factor of the source journal in the publication year included as a regressor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IF often improves prediction but relationship with article-level impact is not strictly linear; include as control (time-invariant) in Reduced and Full models to assess venue effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship: number of authors (AUTH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of authors on the byline included as a continuous predictor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AUTH shows a positive coefficient at very early t but can become negative in later iterations, indicating its effect may change over the publication lifecycle; include and monitor trend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native English-speaking author dummy (D_ENG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dummy variable indicating presence of at least one native English-speaking author in the byline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounts for potential linguistic advantage; initial positive effect that may decline or turn negative over time (observed coefficient trend in Full models).

rubrics_metrics.name: International collaboration dummy (D_FOREIGN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dummy variable for publications with two or more countries in the author affiliation list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International collaboration often correlates with higher citations early on; effect declines over iterations. Be aware of correlation with D_ENG (observed correlation ≈ 0.60).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding acknowledgement dummy (D_FUNDING)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dummy variable indicating publication received financial support (acknowledgement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding often correlates with higher citation rates short-term but predictive power may diminish over time and can show negative trajectories in models; include to capture short-term boosts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access status dummy (D_OPEN: Green/Hybrid/Gold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dummy(s) indicating open access status (Green, Hybrid, Gold) of the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OA articles tend to attract more citations early on, but the OA effect decreases over time. Include OA status especially when predicting short-term citation increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document type controls (D_ART, D_REW)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dummy variables distinguishing articles and reviews from baseline conference proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews typically have higher citation rates; control for document type as these categories are mutually exclusive and affect citation trajectories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication length (PAGES)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of pages of the publication included as an integer predictor (log-transformed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer articles generally receive more citations; include as a control variable (logged) per prior literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference list length (REFER) and reference characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of cited references (REFER) included as predictor; related features include diversity of cited fields, cognitive distance, recency, and presence of highly cited references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer reference lists and inclusion of recent/highly cited references correlate with increased citations. Consider also reference diversity and self-citation proportion where measurable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary classification controls (subject category dummies S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a set of dummy variables representing WoS subject categories (247 dummies in the dataset) to control for field-specific citation dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential because citation patterns differ widely by discipline; necessary to avoid confounding and to normalize impact across heterogeneous fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation and multicollinearity diagnostics
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct descriptive statistics, correlation matrices, autocorrelation analysis, and check Herfindahl-Hirschman Index for category concentration to diagnose multicollinearity and heterogeneity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High autocorrelations among successive impact/readership measures require excluding simultaneous inclusion of all impact variables. No pairwise correlations were high enough to suggest severe multicollinearity among time-invariant variables, but some (e.g., D_FOREIGN vs D_ENG) are notable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid simultaneous inclusion of highly autocorrelated predictors
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include multiple highly autocorrelated measures of the same construct (e.g., IMPACT_t0..t6 simultaneously) in one model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including all impact variables together would produce severe multicollinearity and compromise predictive estimates; instead iterate models replacing the time-varying variable(s) or use dimension reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale readership and impact to field-year averages
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalize READ_t and IMPACT_t by scaling to the average readership/citations of WoS publications in the same subject category and publication year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field-year scaling makes measures comparable across disciplines and publication years and is used consistently for both response and predictors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include only variables measurable at scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer predictors that can be consistently measured across large datasets; acknowledge that some non-quality-related factors cannot be consistently measured at large scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical modeling constraint: exclude or flag features that lack consistent, large-scale measurement even if theoretically relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use coefficient trends across time-iterations to assess evolving predictor influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Trace changes in regression coefficients for each predictor across the t0–t6 iterations to understand how predictor importance evolves with longer short-term windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example findings: L_IMPACT_t coefficient increases from 0.243 (t0) to 0.976 (t6); L_READ_t decreases from 0.278 to 0.070; other variables (AUTH, D_ENG, D_FUNDING, D_OPEN) show distinct trajectories indicating changing roles over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider altmetrics and social media exposure as complementary predictors
rubrics_metrics.description: Altmetrics (tweets, blog mentions, policy citations) can complement traditional predictors but their relationship with long-term citations is complex and field-dependent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early altmetric attention may predict higher citation rates in some contexts (e.g., Eysenbach 2011), but coverage varies by field; include cautiously and interpret results with field-aware controls.
